claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Configuration Section, IV-31' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Nucleus, VI-9'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Configuration Section, IV-31' then '  Nucleus, VI-9'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use '- ' list items). Entries and references match the PDF; informative content.

verdict.reasoning: The claim quotes both sources accurately. The 300 dpi render of PDF page 964 (B-52, Index) prints one entry per line, with sub-entries indented. The transcription (page-964.md) has the same entries and page references, one per line, and indents each sub-entry by two spaces (for example 'Configuration Section, IV-31' then '  Nucleus, VI-9', and 'Control break' with its four sub-entries). No text is missing, misquoted or changed. The only difference is Markdown presentation: the page uses no list markers, while pages 961-962 do, so a renderer may join the lines into one paragraph. The source text keeps every entry boundary and the hierarchy, and the page belongs to the informative index. A formatting difference that does not change meaning is not a content discrepancy. At most it is a style inconsistency across pages.
